description: Proposes bumps to the images the compose files pin. It opens a pull request and nothing else: you merge and deploy, so git still names what runs. See docs/decisions.md, 'Pinned images are bumped by a pull request'.

packageRules.description: One pull request for the sidecar that three deployments carry, so the three move together.
Immich's server and machine-learning images are one version and move together. Taken from the override file only; the vendored upstream file is switched off below.
prBodyNotes: **This PR moves only the two image versions in `deployments/immich/compose.override.yaml`.** Taking a release also means replacing `deployments/immich/compose.yaml` with that release's own file and reading the diff, especially the postgres and valkey `image:` lines, which follow the release (`deployments/immich/SOURCE`). Read Immich's release notes for every version between the old pin and this one before merging.

packageRules.description: deployments/immich/compose.yaml is Immich's release file, unmodified. Its postgres and valkey lines follow that release, not the newest registry tag: the postgres tag names a Postgres major version, so a newer tag can be a dump-and-restore upgrade (Dependabot proposed 14 to 16). deployments/immich/SOURCE says how a release is taken.
Commit-tagged image built by the fork's CI, so there is no version order to follow. Deployed by editing compose.yaml by hand (its README, 'A new version').
Built on `one` from a checkout, never pulled from a registry.
Stopped deployments, kept as files. destiny-director follows a moving tag by design.
